newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senate votes to ban tobacco ads near schools.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senate votes to ban tobacco ads near schools.

text.p: California's Senate voted on Friday to ban cigarette advertising on billboards near schools and playgrounds, in an effort to reduce smoking among children.
The bill, passed 26-6 in the Senate, now requires Republican Gov. Pete Wilson's signature to become law. The state Assembly approved the bill in May.

The legislation, authored by Assemblywoman Carole Migden, would prohibit tobacco products from being advertised on billboards within 1,000 feet of playgrounds as well as elementary, junior high and high schools.
Migden, a Democrat, said her bill was consistent with the recently proposed national settlement of state lawsuits against the tobacco industry, federal regulations and court rulings.
Supporters of the bill said it would help combat tobacco use by minors. Opponents argued that government regulations should be kept to a minimum.
A spokesman for Wilson said the governor had yet to review Migden's bill.
Tobacco companies spent about $200 million in outdoor advertising in 1996, about 10 percent of the industry total, according to the Outdoor Advertising Association of America.
